clue.text: Almost ruin modern housing around 13

definitions.note: the answer to 13 across is STUPID, so this asks for a synonym of stupid

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the assembled letters round, reading them back to front
housing means the word for modern holds the shortened ruin inside it

parts.note: modern means new

indicators.note: almost means the word for ruin loses its final letter

parts.note: ruin means doom

explanation.surface: Someone nearly wrecks a modern house by stuffing it with an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' gives NDOOEW, which 'around' reverses. The definition is a cross-reference: the answer to 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden can mean dull-witted or blockheaded, a sense Chambers gives alongside stiff and lifeless.

clue.text: Gate with card entry deactivated

indicators.note: deactivated, switched off at the start, says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a ticket is a card that grants entry

explanation.surface: A security gate whose card-entry system has been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deactivated' removes T from TICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small gate or door, often set into a larger one.

clue.text: Agreed over experience surrounding single male

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: surrounding means the verb for experience goes around the next pair

parts.note: to find something hard is to experience it so
single means one

explanation.surface: Settled once a single man has had enough experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Of one mind describes people in full accord with each other.

clue.text: Blasphemer, alderman, just a bit green

indicators.note: just a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A list of a blasphemer and an alderman, the latter a bit naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright shade of green, named for the gemstone.

clue.text: Official seat left after court fire

indicators.note: after places the letter for left behind the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: An official loses their seat once the court has fired them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed cushion on which the Lord Speaker sits in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Instrument — gong with hole in it

indicators.note: with, read together with in it, says the award holds the hole
in it means the hole goes inside the award

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or honour such as the OBE
O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: An instrument made of a gong with a hole cut in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is slang for an honour; the OBE is a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument with a double reed.

clue.text: Signs of tuition recently breaking records

indicators.note: breaking means the time word splits the records apart

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
late can mean recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: Students lately have been breaking records.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, red L-plates mark a learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: L-plates are the signs on a car showing the driver is still taking lessons.

clue.text: Extremely agreeable concession for one who told tales

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: A very agreeable concession for a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of the fables.

clue.text: Want to enter tower just above Wellington?

indicators.note: to enter means the word for want goes inside the tower

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
to want is to need

explanation.surface: A desire to get into a tower stands just above the Duke of Wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the Duke, but it is a wellington boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Water knee-deep would come just over the top of a wellington boot.

clue.text: Jail in which you'd chill out

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison or a cell
read literally, a ... is a box or room that chills whatever is put in it

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as relaxing, but taken literally it is something that makes you cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is old slang for prison, and literally any device that chills things.

clue.text: Combine cold beers with retro environmental packaging

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: packaging means the reversed green prefix wraps around the drinks
retro, looking backwards, says the prefix is read in reverse

parts.note: eco- is the prefix meaning environmental
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A drinks firm combines chilled beer with old-style green packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' makes OCE before 'packaging' wraps it round the beers.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to merge or come together into one mass.

clue.text: Refinement, maybe, in English weapon

indicators.note: in places the example marker inside the weapon

parts.note: a lance is a long weapon used by mounted knights
maybe signals an example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: An English weapon perhaps shows a certain refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is grace and polish of style, which is what refinement describes.

clue.text: Made into brass about to get cast

parts.note: ca, circa, is the abbreviation for about
to cast off skin or leaves is to shed it

explanation.surface: Something made into brass is about to be cast in a foundry.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashed means converted into money, and brass is slang for money.

clue.text: Senior copper drives round, missing intelligence

indicators.note: round says the combined letters are turned about and read backwards

parts.note: a DI, detective inspector, is a senior police officer
in golf, drives and putts are both strokes, and puts is used loosely for drives here as sends or propels

explanation.surface: A senior police officer drives around, short on information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns DIPUTS back to front. 'Drives' means puts as in puts or sends something somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stupid lacks brains, so missing intelligence is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: One insect let loose after another

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters behind the other insect

parts.note: another insect here is a bee

indicators.note: let loose means the letters are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: One insect is released after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' turns LET into TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases.

clue.text: Hell to write, breaking through dark as necessary

indicators.note: breaking means the underworld and the writing verb burst into the middle of the other pair

parts.note: in can mean through, by means of
sable is the heraldic word for black, so dark
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Writing about hell is essential, breaking through into darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman underworld; sable is heraldic black. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Indispensable means essential, something you cannot do without.

clue.text: Bishop with sixth sense combed uncovered spot

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ESP, extrasensory perception, is the sixth sense

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: to heckle flax is to comb it out

explanation.surface: A bishop with a sixth sense combs out an exposed blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips H and D from HECKLED, an old word for combing flax.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespeckle is to mark with small spots or flecks.

clue.text: Mature draftee will have done so

definitions.meaning: ..., as in ... thinking or writing, means grown-up and coherent
a draftee has ..., enlisted in the forces

explanation.surface: An older conscript will already have enlisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined-up describes adult coherent thinking, and to join up is to sign on for military service.

clue.text: Sod's Law — I've let out unsubstantiated info

indicators.note: out signals the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone groans that Murphy's Law strikes again and lets slip a rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles SODSLAWIVELET; Sod's Law is the British name for Murphy's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wives' tales are traditional beliefs passed on without any evidence behind them.

clue.text: Tough guy inviting female interpretation?

indicators.note: inviting, with interpretation, asks the solver to decode the answer itself as wordplay
interpretation says the answer is read as an instruction whose result is the clue word

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: iron gives its chemical symbol and man gives a synonym, which together spell this clue word

explanation.surface: A macho man is asking to be seen from a woman's point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue, which 'inviting ... interpretation' flags: FE (iron's chemical symbol) + MALE (man) spell 'female'.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron man is someone of great physical strength and endurance.

clue.text: In which a Callas cast?

indicators.note: cast means the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Where would Maria Callas be cast in an opera?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges ACALLAS; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is the opera house where soprano Maria Callas famously sang.

clue.text: Aim to block attempt to get in

indicators.note: to block means the aim sits inside the attempt, blocking it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An aim to block an attempt to get inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the definition, as in fashionable; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable, as does trendy.

clue.text: One won't turn up to eat without coming back

parts.note: to nosh is informal for to eat

indicators.note: coming back says the abbreviation is reversed

explanation.surface: A guest won't arrive to eat without coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses WO, the short form for without, to OW.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a person who fails to appear for a booking or appointment.

clue.text: Unintroduced loan shark is more confident

indicators.note: unintroduced means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a usurer lends at extortionate interest, like a loan shark

explanation.surface: A loan shark who has not been introduced is all the more confident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unintroduced' drops U from USURER. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Surer is the comparative of sure, meaning more certain.

clue.text: Blokes curse boxers et al

parts.note: blokes is British slang for men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Male fighters swear at each other in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' looks like fighters, but it is boxer shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts and similar garments are examples of clothing for men.

clue.text: Confuse at least the weekend broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard over the airwaves, a sound-alike

parts.note: the weekend is two days, so at least the weekend means days

explanation.surface: Confusion is broadcast all weekend at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals a sound-alike: DAYS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze is to stun or bewilder someone.

clue.text: Mark date for operating on thighs?

indicators.note: operating on, as a surgeon works on a body, signals the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A surgeon notes the date for an operation on someone's thighs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operating on' shuffles MARKDATE. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken thighs and legs are the cuts called dark meat; the question mark marks thighs as an example.

clue.text: Flashing when naked is a piece of cake

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: flashing, giving off sparks, means sparking

explanation.surface: Flashing in the nude is described as easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when naked' strips S and G from SPARKING. Parkin is a ginger oatmeal cake from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a sticky cake, so a slice of it is literally a piece of cake.

clue.text: Was mum perhaps torn between dad and, ultimately, love child?

indicators.note: between puts the word for torn in the gap after the father figure

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letters of the next two words

parts.note: torn means rent, as in ripped

explanation.surface: A mother wonders whether she was caught between the father and her beloved child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' covers both love and child. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a mum is one way to have raised a child, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Acting like China, welcoming European in insipid fashion

indicators.note: welcoming means the friendly word takes the European letter in

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so acting like a china is being pally

explanation.surface: China courts a European partner in a rather feeble way.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Palely means wanly or weakly, without colour or spirit.
